text:
Priya: heads-up from tonight's int8 bring-up: our canary harness shows sporadic funcall corruption under bursty load
Dan: what do you mean by corruption? examples?
Priya: small sample from proxy stdout (payload tails are base64-encoded to show control chars)
```
RECV 2026-03-18T01:02:10Z id=xyz789 body="{\"tool\":\"lookup\",\"args\":[{\"id\":123}] }
SEND 2026-03-18T01:02:10Z id=xyz789 tail_b64="WyJfX0VORF9fIl0=
"
RECV 2026-03-18T01:02:10Z id=xyz790 body="{\"tool\":\"lookup\",\"args\":[{\"id\":124}],\u0000"
ERROR parse id=xyz790 Reason=trailing_controlchar
```
Lee: WyJfX0VORF9fIl0= is just base64("["__END__"]") interesting that one has proper sentinel and the other has embedded NUL at end
Nina: are these coming from the model runtime, the streaming proxy, or the HTTP layer?
Priya: narrowed to chunked responses from the runtime when requests overlap. If two chunks flush back-to-back and the serializer preempts, we sometimes see half a UTF-8 sequence or stray \u0000 bytes inserted
Dan: could be related to the ptq runtime's output buffer reuse. We recently switched to yield-based flushing which reuses a shared slice without zeroing
Priya: exactly. Repro: hit with 200 qps, concurrency 60, run for 10k requests -> ~0.6% malformed toolcalls, mostly missing closing bracket or NUL suffix
Lee: mitigation ideas: 1) zero-copy is nice but we can clone final chunk before enqueueing, 2) turn on TCP_NODELAY on the proxy to avoid coalescing, 3) sentinel + client-side parse guard, 4) server returns 503 on partial stream so client can retry
Nina: I vote for short-term server-side 503 for partials + telemetry. Long-term we should fix slice reuse in runtime. Also add a canary config knob: max_inflight_for_model=20
infra-bot: canary deployment 2026-03-18T01:00 rolled: canary-config(max_inflight_for_model=20) applied by ci/canary
Dan: small experiment: I added a debug wrapper to the runtime that memsets last byte to 0xFF before handing to serializer. Malformed drops to 0.05% in 50k run -> indicates memory re-use bug
Priya: nice. Can we detect corrupted UTF-8 at serialization boundary and reject earlier? That would cause detectable 5xx and trigger client retry instead of opaque parse errors downstream
Lee: yes, add a final UTF-8 validity + sentinel check. If failed emit metric funcall_boundary_corruption and return 502. Also log first 64 bytes of tail in telemetry (redact PII)
Nina: create an eng-ml postmortem template entry and add on-call instruction: if funcall_boundary_corruption > 1% for 10m, page priority-2 to @eng-runtime and @infra
Priya: filed quicknote: https://redwood.internal/notes/int8-chunk-boundary-20260318 (internal) with repro script and sample logs
Dan: plan of record: (A) backport runtime slice fix, (B) add sentinel + UTF-8 validation + 502 gate, (C) throttle canary parallelism to 20 until fix lands, (D) nightly stress 200k to verify
Lee: i'll open PR for (B) and add telemetry dims model_variant, quant_mode, canary_parallel, raw_tail_prefix_b64
infra-bot: alert muted by Nina for this thread
Nina: thanks all. we caught this before customer traffic. small ask: include a one-liner in the PR desc about why zeroing is unsafe with shared slices so future reviewers notice
Priya: will do. closing loop after PR lands and nightly passes.
